A hands-on short course for researchers, public health professionals and
students. Lectures alternate with practical work.

By the end you will be able to choose a study design, compute the measures that
design gives you, read them correctly, tell a real effect from a biased one,
and do all of it in R.

## Before you arrive
There are 5 steps to work through before Monday 21 September. They take about
3 hours. Spread them over a few evenings.

Installing the software is the only step we cannot fix for you on the day.

→ [**Start here: the 5 steps**](prelude/index.qmd)

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
The programme is being finalised and will be circulated separately.
:::

## What you will be able to do

::: {.card-grid}

::: {.card-tile}
### Measure disease
Turn counts into prevalence, risk, rate and person-time. Say which one a
question needs.
:::

::: {.card-tile}
### Measure association
Build a 2×2 table. Read a risk ratio, an odds ratio, a risk difference and a
number needed to treat off it.
:::

::: {.card-tile}
### Choose a design
Match a question to a cohort, case-control, cross-sectional or trial design.
Know what each one can and cannot tell you.
:::

::: {.card-tile}
### Spot bias
Name the bias in front of you: selection, information, confounding. Tell
confounding from interaction.
:::

::: {.card-tile}
### Analyse in R
Import, clean, summarise and plot data with the tidyverse, instead of clicking
through a menu you cannot document.
:::

::: {.card-tile}
### Work reproducibly
Organise an analysis so that a colleague, a reviewer, or you in six months can
rerun every number from the raw data.
:::

:::

## Who this is for

Researchers, public health professionals, programme managers and students.

No programming is assumed. If you have used SPSS, Excel or Stata, you already
know most of the statistical ideas. This course changes the tools and sharpens
the reasoning.

You need a laptop you can install software on, and about 3 hours before the
course for the [5 steps](prelude/index.qmd).

## How to use this site

- **[Before you arrive](prelude/index.qmd)**. 5 steps: install R and RStudio,
  install the packages, work through the R primers, then the epidemiology
  primers, then browse the resources. Start here.
- **[Resources](resources/index.qmd)**. Cheatsheet, troubleshooting, glossary
  and further reading. Use these during the course and after it.

All materials stay online after the course. The site is built from a public
repository, so corrections are welcome as issues or pull requests.
